text: A package running is one thing. Knowing what it actually did — or is doing right now — is another. This lesson is about the tools SSMS gives you to monitor SSISDB execution.

Everything writes to one place: the SSISDB database. For what's happening right now, right-click SSISDB and open Active Operations — every running deployment, validation, and execution, with a Stop button. For history, it's Reports, Standard Reports: the Integration Services Dashboard for the last 24 hours with drill-down links into Overview, All Messages, and Execution Performance, plus All Executions for any date range you want, complete with the exact parameter values each run used.

Here's the direct payoff from Lesson 44's logging level decision: the Execution Performance report's per-component timing breakdown — genuinely useful for finding your slowest transformation — only shows up if that run's logging level was set to Performance or Verbose. Leave it at the default Basic, and that detail was never recorded in the first place, no matter how badly you need it after the fact.
That wraps up Chapter 8. Next, the capstone — building a real end-to-end ETL package that pulls together everything from control flow through deployment.
